epics.title: LLM-Authored Projections, Accessibility & Non-Visual Interfaces
epics.goal: Let deterministic Ignite behavior support accessible DOM, text, speech, terminal, and agent-authored interfaces by storing validated projection documents in actor state, exposing authoring commands through igniteTools, and keeping generic inspection, binding, and committer machinery private.
acceptance: The superseded ProjectionRequest/ProjectionSpec registry and command-presentation-metadata design ships no source implementation and remains historical only.

igniteCore keeps its existing source/view/commands/events/effects configuration and custom-element registrar without public registry, bind, inspect, behavior metadata, or adapter-wide projection generics.
Private coherent inspection plus generic projection/binding/committer machinery supports format-specific output without requiring DOM for speech, terminal, or agent paths.

Validated ProjectionDocument data with stable ids, safe semantic nodes, and command-backed actions lives in actor state; raw generated JSX, JavaScript, imports, event handlers, and DOM references are rejected.
LLMs author and incrementally patch projection documents through igniteTools commands, while actor state and command availability remain authoritative.

A voice/text control-center proves prompt or speech input through model tool calls to durable projection state, accessible native JSX, and model-authored speech/text with deterministic CI and optional MLX validation.
Headless tests prove behavior and document contracts; rendered tests separately prove keyboard, focus, accessible names, relationships, and intentional live output.
Final docs teach the minimal public DX, provider/privacy boundaries, actor-web behavior graph alignment, and why voice does not require JSX or DOM.

epics.title: Retained Surfaces and Complex Interface Runtime
epics.goal: Make Ignite Element support canvas, WebGL, editors, maps, video, and high-frequency dashboards through typed callback refs, reserved post-reconciliation commit directives, keyed reconciliation, move-safe resource lifecycle, and evidence-driven scheduling decisions while preserving the existing igniteCore registration API and source authority.
acceptance: The architecture defines a generic retained-surface contract rather than a canvas-specific core API, with source state remaining authoritative and effects remaining consequence-oriented.

Ignite JSX provides typed callback refs and a reserved commit directive with deterministic initial, update, replacement, move, and true-disconnect cleanup semantics without leaking directives to the DOM.
Keyed reconciliation preserves canvas contexts, editor instances, focus, selection, and other retained node state through reorder and fallback paths.
igniteCore gains no commitScheduling surface; retained resources own requestAnimationFrame or microtask cadence until post-dogfood evidence demonstrates a need at the component registration boundary.

A deterministic real-time canvas stress example proves device-pixel-ratio sizing, ResizeObserver handling, consumer-owned requestAnimationFrame interpolation, scoped input, telemetry, and accessible DOM companions.

Downstream validation documents the Actor-Web Mesh Pong adoption contract without moving Actor-Web lifecycle, simulation, transport, or advisory authority into Ignite, and a later evidence task records the no-API verdict or creates a separate scheduler implementation brief.

The model-turn, voice-capture, and speech-delivery workflows have one authoritative owner with typed events, effects, facts, raw snapshots, and derived views.
Any Ignite graph-testing bridge is optional, XState-specific, dogfood-justified, additive to igniteTest, and does not create a second graph engine, recorder, schema, or state authority.

epics.title: Voice Workbench Hexagonal Boundary Conformance

Deterministic domain, policy, reducer, actor protocol, and pure projection modules depend only inward on example-owned serializable contracts and contain no browser, Node, provider, clock, network, randomness, or concrete adapter work.

The model-turn application path uses a framework-neutral actor-backed command and read-model port; browser, terminal, and headless model execution do not require an Ignite component as runtime authority.
MLX, web search, product pricing, microphone, speech, time, and environment behavior live in replaceable imperative adapters that translate expected outcomes into correlated facts or receipts.
Ignite composition contains projection and command binding only; renderer functions consume renderer-neutral prepared views and return JSX/templates without workflow derivation or effects.

Every explicit Voice Workbench state machine has a source-aligned contract and independent bounded validation receipt covering reachability, event disposition, terminal and recovery paths, forbidden states, serialization, correlation, and supervision.
Executable import-boundary, forbidden-global, graph, headless, browser, terminal, parity, accessibility, replay, cleanup, and full verification gates pass with zero reviewed architecture violations.

A behavior-complete specimen-first Mock Studio foundation precedes a fresh visual round; MagicPath revision 9 remains historical donor-only evidence, and explicit human approval gates any new visual synthesis and the technical POC.

The browser and Vitest consume the same browser-safe shared Story modules through the existing igniteTest story API; browser code never imports test files.

Every run uses a fresh real target runtime and any real machine or actor owned by the specimen while clocks, providers, network, microphone, speech, and other nondeterministic boundaries are controlled through fixture-owned ports.

Run, Step, Cancel, Restart, and Back via dispose, rebuild, and replay expose transient page facts, snapshots, semantic views, command availability, assertions, timing telemetry, semantic context diffs, and only the ordinary final Story receipt after completion.

An optional XState lens projects topology, active parallel nodes, monotonic observations, snapshot deltas, candidate or uniquely evidenced edges, and only directly provable trigger, guard, or branch labels without moving graph ownership into Ignite.

Bidirectional narrative, state, transition, and page coverage joins explicit stable catalog IDs, declared direct-test evidence, optional topology, and ordered observations while surfacing unavailable, uncovered, excluded, invariant-only, private-system, projection-only, and expected-no-change dispositions honestly.

The accepted Mock Studio handoff defines the repo catalog, bounded specimen canvas, Story/page/public-command branch lane, docked Inspector, token-driven presentation, responsive anatomy, keyboard and focus behavior, reduced motion, failure and no-lens states, and measurable parity targets for the dev/test workbench host.

The product remains example-local for the MVP, defaults to component and feature-projection specimens, labels full-page or composed Voice Workbench surfaces as integration specimens, adds no package or public Ignite API, owns no runtime state or replacement trace, and keeps MagicPath preview, rendered DOM, manual browser, headless Story, graph, and machine evidence distinct.

Deterministic-within-a-controlled-envelope replay, fixture isolation, stale-session suppression, exact cleanup, browser accessibility, adapter-neutral no-lens behavior, and a versioned JSON-safe CI and LLM review artifact are verified incrementally across admitted specimens; broader Voice Workbench Story dogfooding remains a later integration-specimen phase.

epics.title: Source-only provisioning and host-boundary standard
epics.goal: Make exact native sources the canonical application composition boundary across browser, Node, test, XState, Redux, MobX, Actor-Web, and custom runtimes: applications bind capability ports through source-library-native APIs, native source lifecycles own environmental cleanup, igniteCore receives only the resulting source, and retained presentation resources remain in renderer ref and commit lifecycle.
acceptance: A durable architecture standard defines ports, adapters, exact native sources, source-native provisioning, native lifecycle ownership, commands, effects, renderer ref and commit, igniteShell, and headless boundaries without introducing createFeature or another wrapper vocabulary.
igniteCore gains no driver, environment, ports, provisioning, disposal, Feature, or lifecycle-wrapper surface and receives the exact XState, Redux, MobX, Actor-Web, or custom source.
Routing, Redux, MobX, Actor-Web, Node/headless, and deterministic fake examples bind ports through native source APIs and prove cleanup through each source ecosystem native lifecycle.
Commands express intent without host access; effects publish accepted outward facts without owning environmental I/O, source lifecycle, or retained presentation resources.
ref acquires and cleans up stable node-bound resources while commit synchronizes current projected data after reconciliation; neither callback creates, wraps, stops, or disposes the source.

Public docs and migration guidance teach the source-only pattern with automated conformance evidence and link to the separate retained-interface contract for Canvas, Cytoscape, editors, and similar resources.

epics.title: Evidence-Governed Runtime Projections
epics.goal: Consume versioned Actor-Web execution, admission, session, and reconciliation evidence as optional external facts; project it through Ignite without acquiring runtime authority; prove freshness, replay, recovery, and FAS evidence compatibility; and issue an evidence-backed public API verdict.
acceptance: Actor-Web remains the authority for authenticated admission, execution receipts, durable sessions, retries, replay, and reconciliation while Ignite consumes and projects versioned facts only.

The optional Actor-Web adapter fails closed on unsupported or malformed evidence and preserves upstream principal, intent, correlation, attempt, revision, sequence, and receipt identity without duplicating authority.
Projected capability and canExecute state remains descriptive preflight; the authoritative runtime rechecks command, payload, principal, approval, revision, idempotency, and policy at execution time.
Ignite Story evidence and Actor-Web execution receipts remain distinct, provenance-bearing channels joined through an explicit source-of-truth matrix rather than a second trace or receipt authority.
Voice Workbench and Ignite Alchemy dogfood stale authorization, revision rejection, timeout, retry, cancellation, restart, replay, partial failure, and reconciliation using the same neutral contract.
FAS consumes versioned fixture evidence through its existing optional adapters without becoming an Ignite or Actor-Web runtime dependency.
No new public Ignite inspection, orchestration, blueprint, or receipt API ships unless dogfood demonstrates a concrete gap and a separate compatibility review accepts it.
